answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 7 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The garden multiplier is published, charged in island, and canyon lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4903 identities would post 4675 proofs and burn roughly 33 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
